target: Dişçiye dişimi çektirdim.
english: I had my tooth pulled by the dentist.
tip: 'çektirdim' adds -tir- to 'çekmek' so it means I had it pulled, not I pulled. The doer takes the dative, here 'dişçiye' (by the dentist).

target: Güneş açınca mont giydim.
english: When the sun came out, I put on my coat.
tip: Adding -ınca to a verb means once or when it happens. 'açınca' is once it opened, said of the sun coming out.

target: Üçte bir oranında indirim var.
english: There is a one-third discount.
tip: Turkish builds fractions backwards. 'üçte bir' is literally in three, one, which means one third.

target: Hafta sonu tiyatroya gitmeyi planlıyoruz.
english: We are planning to go to the theater this weekend.
tip: When a verb is the object of another verb it takes -meyi. 'gitmeyi planlıyoruz' is we are planning to go.

target: Hasta oldum, bugün işe gidemeyeceğim.
english: I got sick, I won't be able to go to work today.
tip: 'gidemeyeceğim' stacks -eme, meaning cannot, onto the future, so it is I will not be able to go.

target: Kedi yatağın altında uyuyor, çok tatlı.
english: The cat is sleeping under the bed, so cute.
tip: To say under something, the object takes genitive and 'alt' takes a location ending. 'yatağın altında' is under the bed.

target: Dedemin dükkânı kapatması bizi çok üzdü.
english: My grandfather closing his shop made us very sad.
tip: To turn a whole action into a noun, the doer takes genitive and the verb takes -ması. 'dedemin kapatması' is my grandfather's closing.

target: Annemi doğum gününü kutlamak için aradım.
english: I called my mother to wish her a happy birthday.
tip: 'için' after a plain -mak verb means in order to. 'kutlamak için' is in order to celebrate.

target: Dün gece uyuyamadığım için geç uyandım.
english: I woke up late because I could not sleep last night.
tip: To say because, put -dığı için on the verb. 'uyuyamadığım için' is because I could not sleep.

target: Her akşam ailece televizyon karşısında oturuyoruz.
english: Every evening we sit together as a family in front of the TV.
tip: The suffix -ce on a group means all together as that group. 'ailece' is as a whole family.

target: Erken yatmış olsaydım bu kadar yorgun olmazdım.
english: If I had gone to bed early I wouldn't be this tired.
tip: For an unreal past, use -mış olsaydı in the if part. 'yatmış olsaydım' is if I had gone to bed.

target: Annem telefon edip beni aradığında ben zaten evden çıkmıştım.
english: When my mother called me on the phone I had already left the house.
tip: -mıştım marks an action already finished before another past moment. 'çıkmıştım' is I had already left.

target: Burada Türkçe ve İngilizce konuşulur.
english: Turkish and English are spoken here.
tip: 'konuşulur' adds the passive -ul- to 'konuşmak', so it means are spoken with no named speaker.

target: Bu sınıftaki en çalışkan öğrenci Ali'dir.
english: The most hardworking student in this class is Ali.
tip: Put 'en' before an adjective to make the most. 'en çalışkan' is the most hardworking.

target: Tarlada ekilen buğday hasat zamanını bekliyor.
english: The wheat planted in the field is waiting for harvest time.
tip: -en turns a verb into an adjective sitting before its noun. 'ekilen buğday' is the wheat that was planted.

target: Altıncı kata çıkın, müdürün ofisi orada.
english: Go up to the sixth floor, the director's office is there.
tip: Add -ıncı to a number to make the ordinal. 'altı' becomes 'altıncı', the sixth.

target: Köyün havası şehre göre çok daha temiz.
english: The village air is much cleaner compared to the city.
tip: 'göre' after a dative noun means compared to, and 'daha' marks the comparison. 'şehre göre daha temiz' is cleaner than the city.

target: Kütüphanenin nerede olduğunu biliyor musun?
english: Do you know where the library is?
tip: 'nerede olduğunu' packs where it is into one noun-like clause; the subject 'kütüphanenin' takes genitive -nin.

target: Çocuk merdivenden düşüp sakatlandı.
english: The child fell from the stairs and got injured.
tip: The -ip on 'düşüp' links it to 'sakatlandı'; only the last verb carries the tense, and both share the subject.

target: Haritaya baksaydık yolumuzu kaybetmezdik.
english: If we had looked at the map we wouldn't have gotten lost.
tip: 'baksaydık' is the past unreal, if we had looked; the result 'kaybetmezdik' means we wouldn't have lost.

target: Sınıf arkadaşlarımla yıllar sonra buluştuk.
english: I met up with my classmates after years.
tip: The -la on 'arkadaşlarımla' means with; the suffixes stack as 'arkadaş-lar-ım-la', friends-my-with.

target: Çantamı masanın altına koydum, görmüyor musun?
english: I put my bag under the table, can't you see?
tip: Position words put the owner in genitive: 'masanın altına' means to under the table, with -a marking motion toward.

target: Bugünkü işini yarına bırakma, hemen yap.
english: Don't leave today's work for tomorrow, do it right away.
tip: A negative command adds -ma to the bare verb: 'bırak' means leave, 'bırakma' means don't leave.

target: Bu ilaç reçetesiz satılmaz, doktora gidin.
english: This medicine is not sold without prescription, go to the doctor.
tip: The -siz ending means without: 'reçete' is prescription, 'reçetesiz' means without a prescription.

target: Ne kadar çok okursan o kadar çok öğrenirsin.
english: The more you read, the more you learn.
tip: The frame 'ne kadar ... o kadar' means the more ... the more, pairing 'okursan' with 'öğrenirsin'.

target: Param olsa bile o kadar pahalı araba almam.
english: Even if I had money I wouldn't buy such an expensive car.
tip: -sa plus 'bile' means even if: 'olsa bile' is even if there were, so 'param olsa bile' means even if I had money.

target: Yaşlandıkça insan hayata farklı bir gözle bakmaya başlıyor.
english: As one grows older, one starts to look at life with different eyes.
tip: The -dıkça ending means as one does X, the more: 'yaşlandıkça' means as one grows older.

target: Nefes almak bile zorlaşıyor bu sıcakta.
english: Even breathing gets difficult in this heat.
tip: The -laş ending turns an adjective into become: 'zor' is hard, so 'zorlaşıyor' means is getting hard.

target: Bu binanın yüz elli dairesi var.
english: This building has one hundred fifty apartments.
tip: Ownership is genitive owner plus possessed plus 'var': 'binanın ... dairesi var' means the building has apartments.

target: Her yıl binlerce turist tarafından ziyaret edilir.
english: It is visited by thousands of tourists every year.
tip: In a passive, the doer is named with 'tarafından', by: 'turist tarafından ziyaret edilir', is visited by tourists.
